findings.security_consequence: A verifier that checks only CALL success could continue with empty output; whether that affects proof acceptance depends on its output checks.

findings.divergence: A read-only CREATE simulation on Somnia produced 24,577 runtime bytes with a 120M-gas call; Ethereum's control rejected the 24,577-byte child.
findings.security_consequence: A factory relying on Ethereum's 24,576-byte bound needs a target deployment test; this simulation does not establish transaction admission.
findings.review_action: Price the operation with the target fee oracle and charging rule; do not infer cost from Ethereum gas alone.

findings.divergence: A read-only CREATE simulation with 49,153-byte init code created a child on monad; Ethereum's same control returned an outer execution error. Monad's documented 128 KiB runtime-code cap does not establish its init-code limit.
findings.security_consequence: A factory using init code above Ethereum's 49,152-byte boundary needs a target deployment test; the simulation alone does not prove transaction admission.
findings.review_action: Test the target's init and runtime boundaries with a target-chain deployment gate.

findings.divergence: The same-call funded SELFDESTRUCT kill returned status 0 on zksync-era, while Ethereum returned status 1; the child still had 174 code bytes in the returned state. The zero-value kill also failed and an isolated SELFDESTRUCT init-code call reverted on both reviewed endpoints.
findings.security_consequence: The tested SELFDESTRUCT paths failed closed on zkSync Era; cleanup logic must check the kill status and cannot infer post-transaction deletion from this read-only call.

findings.divergence: Kaia's read-only one-wei identity-precompile CALL returned status 0 and spent no value; Ethereum returned status 1 and spent one wei.

findings.review_action: Run the known-answer vector at the target address and treat empty success as a distinct result.
